name: Quantum-linked telescope array
subtitle: telescopes joined into one giant eye by entanglement

effects.effect: measuring one entangled particle instantly fixes its partner's state, and any snooping shows

effect: measuring one entangled particle instantly fixes its partner's state, and any snooping shows
how: Combining the light of telescopes kilometres apart would be sharp enough to see the surfaces of nearby stars and planets, but faint starlight is lost if piped over long distances. Each telescope instead meets the incoming starlight with one half of an entangled pair shared ahead of time, so the stations combine their light as if joined by a perfect fibre, acting as one telescope kilometres wide.
obstacle: It needs entangled photons as fast as starlight arrives and quantum memories that do not exist yet.
why: Proposed in 2012; only table-top tests so far.
real: Proof-of-principle entanglement/memory-assisted interferometers over 1.55-20 km fibre with lab light (Harvard, USTC 2025), but no telescope or on-sky use.
